# Sirach Chapter 1 — The EMET Bible (Literal)

**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Codex Vaticanus, Sirach 1 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/SIR_001_page_001.jpg

---

**1:1** All wisdom is from the Lord, and with him it remains forever.

**1:2** The sand of the seas and the drops of rain, and the days of eternity — who can number these?

**1:3** The height of heaven and the breadth of the earth and the deep — who can search these out?

**1:4** Wisdom was created before all things, and understanding prudence from eternity.

**1:5** The word of God on high is the fountain of wisdom, and her ways are the everlasting commandments.

**1:6** To whom has the root of wisdom been revealed? And who has understood her clever devices?

**1:7** To whom has the knowledge of wisdom been made known? And who has comprehended her great experience?

**1:8** There is one who is wise, greatly to be feared, sitting upon his throne — the Lord.

**1:9** He himself created her and saw her and numbered her, and he poured her out upon all his works.

**1:10** She is with all flesh according to his gift, and he supplied her freely to those who love him.

**1:11** The fear of the Lord is glory and exultation, and gladness and a crown of rejoicing.

**1:12** The fear of the Lord delights the heart, and gives gladness and joy and long life.

**1:13** With him who fears the Lord it will go well at the end; on the day of his death he will be blessed.

**1:14** The beginning of wisdom is to fear the Lord, and with the faithful she was created in the womb.

**1:15** She has made a nest among human beings an eternal foundation, and among their seed she will be trusted.

**1:16** Fullness of wisdom is to fear the Lord; she makes them drink from the fruit of her deeds.

**1:17** She fills their whole house with what is desirable, and their storehouses with her produce.

**1:18** The crown of wisdom is the fear of the Lord, causing peace and full health to flourish.

**1:19** He rained down knowledge and discerning understanding, and he exalted the glory of those who hold her fast.

**1:20** The root of wisdom is to fear the Lord, and her branches are long life.

**1:21** The fear of the Lord drives away sins; and where it abides it turns away wrath.

**1:22** An unjust man will not be able to justify himself, for the bent of his wrath will be his downfall.

**1:23** A patient man will hold out until the right time, and afterward gladness will burst forth for him.

**1:24** Until the right time he will restrain his words, and the lips of many will tell of his understanding.

**1:25** In the treasuries of wisdom are sayings of instruction, but abomination to a sinner is the worship of God.

**1:26** If you desire wisdom, keep the commandments, and the Lord will supply her freely to you.

**1:27** For the fear of the Lord is wisdom and instruction, and he delights in faithfulness and meekness.

**1:28** Do not disobey the fear of the Lord; do not approach him with a divided heart.

**1:29** Do not play the hypocrite before the eyes of men; watch your lips.

**1:30** Do not exalt yourself lest you fall and bring dishonor upon your soul; the Lord will reveal your secrets and cast you down in the midst of the congregation, because you did not come near to the fear of the Lord, and your heart was full of deceit.

---

*Translator's Note: v.5 is present in some manuscripts but absent from others (absent in the main Vaticanus tradition). Included here with note. Verses 7 and 21 are similarly textually uncertain. Greek phobos kyriou ("fear of the Lord") rendered consistently throughout as "fear of the Lord."*
